result.summary: DO-NOT-SHIP: pass 4 found four blocking failure paths in edd7aa5. This was a read-only source review; the current head was not run on Windows.

findings.title: 1. BLOCKING — cancel can still overwrite a terminal record
findings.body: The win32 terminal check runs before `withStateLock`. A concurrent reaper can mark the job failed while cancel waits for that lock. Inside the lock, cancel rereads the terminal file but unconditionally spreads `nextJob` over it and writes `cancelled`, losing the failure result.
findings.recommendation: Check terminal status inside the lock before deleting artifacts or writing, and return the stored result.

findings.title: 2. BLOCKING — a terminal race hides kill survivors
findings.body: After a kill returns 243 with survivors, another command can reap the dead worker before this check. `finishedBeforeCancel` then returns with `cancellationPending:false`, no survivor identities, and exit 0. The documented unbounded leak is hidden even though this cancel invocation observed it.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the terminal record, but report the observed kill failure and survivors with a nonzero exit.

findings.title: 3. BLOCKING — a child can evade cancel by mentioning the broker marker
findings.body: Any verified worker child whose command line contains `app-server-broker.mjs` is excluded, along with its subtree, without proof that it is the shared broker. A job can launch an unrelated long-running child with that argument; cancel kills the worker, then leaves that child alive with no later orphan cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Replace the command-line exemption with broker ownership established before spawn; refuse and retry during an unrecorded start window.

findings.title: 4. BLOCKING — failed broker start can discard ownership of a live subtree
findings.body: If the tree kill fails, the fallback `child.kill` stops only the broker root. The new wait verifies only that root, then clears its provisional record even though the broker may already have spawned an app-server child; the test fixture explicitly models that descendant. If the root stays alive instead, the kept record still has `pidIdentity:null` despite a completed identity probe, and stale replacement later drops it without a verified kill.
findings.recommendation: Persist a successful identity probe immediately, retain ownership data after failed teardown, and clear it only after verifying the whole spawned tree exited.

next_steps: Fix the terminal-state race and preserve survivor reporting.
Replace marker-based broker shielding and close failed-start ownership gaps.
Run targeted Windows E2E races and the CI matrix on the corrected commit.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP: pass 4 found four blocking failure paths in edd7aa5. This was a read-only source review; the current head was not run on Windows.

Findings:
- [high] 1. BLOCKING — cancel can still overwrite a terminal record (plugins/codex/scripts/codex-companion.mjs:1392-1404)
  The win32 terminal check runs before `withStateLock`. A concurrent reaper can mark the job failed while cancel waits for that lock. Inside the lock, cancel rereads the terminal file but unconditionally spreads `nextJob` over it and writes `cancelled`, losing the failure result.
  Recommendation: Check terminal status inside the lock before deleting artifacts or writing, and return the stored result.
- [high] 2. BLOCKING — a terminal race hides kill survivors (plugins/codex/scripts/codex-companion.mjs:1357-1362)
  After a kill returns 243 with survivors, another command can reap the dead worker before this check. `finishedBeforeCancel` then returns with `cancellationPending:false`, no survivor identities, and exit 0. The documented unbounded leak is hidden even though this cancel invocation observed it.
  Recommendation: Preserve the terminal record, but report the observed kill failure and survivors with a nonzero exit.
- [high] 3. BLOCKING — a child can evade cancel by mentioning the broker marker (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/process.mjs:502-507)
  Any verified worker child whose command line contains `app-server-broker.mjs` is excluded, along with its subtree, without proof that it is the shared broker. A job can launch an unrelated long-running child with that argument; cancel kills the worker, then leaves that child alive with no later orphan cleanup.
  Recommendation: Replace the command-line exemption with broker ownership established before spawn; refuse and retry during an unrecorded start window.
- [high] 4. BLOCKING — failed broker start can discard ownership of a live subtree (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:304-326)
  If the tree kill fails, the fallback `child.kill` stops only the broker root. The new wait verifies only that root, then clears its provisional record even though the broker may already have spawned an app-server child; the test fixture explicitly models that descendant. If the root stays alive instead, the kept record still has `pidIdentity:null` despite a completed identity probe, and stale replacement later drops it without a verified kill.
  Recommendation: Persist a successful identity probe immediately, retain ownership data after failed teardown, and clear it only after verifying the whole spawned tree exited.

Next steps:
- Fix the terminal-state race and preserve survivor reporting.
- Replace marker-based broker shielding and close failed-start ownership gaps.
- Run targeted Windows E2E races and the CI matrix on the corrected commit.
